findings.certainty: high on the mechanism (one unpriced request permanently makes the session total unavailable); medium that this conflicts with the confirmed intent (estimate is deliberately withheld whenever completeness is in doubt, so this may be an accepted design consequence rather than a defect).
findings.evidence: beginSessionCostRequest is called once at the start of every processStreamEvents (SSEStream.swift:275) regardless of provider and unconditionally does request_count+1 and unpriced_count+1 (SessionCostLedger.swift:64, via ChatStore.swift:4255-4260); for a non-DeepSeek or interrupted/completed=false request no DeepSeekCostRecord is written (AIChatViewModel+Billing.swift:37-44, SSEStream.swift:1010 passes completed:_streamError == nil && result.stopReason != nil), so unpriced_count is never decremented; SessionCostSummary.estimatedAmountCNY returns nil whenever unpricedCount != 0 (SessionCostLedger.swift:8), and the UI then renders “—” for Estimated Session Cost even though real DeepSeek requests with known amounts are already summed in amount_cny. SessionCostLedgerTests.testInterruptedOrUnsupportedRequestDoesNotBecomeFree pins this “whole-total becomes nil” semantics.

findings.trigger: In one session, send any main-chat request that is not a priced official-DeepSeek request (e.g. switch to another OpenAI-compatible model, or have a request interrupted/retried, fail mid-stream, or fall outside the supported 2026 pricing calendar), then switch back to the official DeepSeek model and open the context capsule.
findings.verification: Static cross-file read of the four files plus the ledger test; no execution. The mechanism is deterministic from the code; whether the permanent suppression after switching back is intended is a requirements-reading judgement, not something the code or tests settle (the acceptance list only specifies “—” for the non-DeepSeek case and does not state whether the DeepSeek total must reappear when the user returns to DeepSeek).

findings.certainty: medium (code behaviour is certain; the practical frequency and whether the vendor ever omits the fields is unverified).
findings.evidence: parse computes `let cached = count(details?["cached_tokens"] ?? usage["prompt_cache_hit_tokens"])` and then requires `guard let input = …, let output = …, let cached = …, cached <= input else { return nil }` (DeepSeekRequestUsage.swift:16-22); a missing cache field therefore yields nil instead of cacheReadTokens = 0, so no DeepSeekCostRecord is produced. Combined with R1 this hides the entire session estimate rather than slightly over- or under-estimating one request. The test suite only exercises cache fields that are present-but-invalid (SessionCostLedgerTests.swift:115-125: missing completion_tokens, hit > prompt, inconsistent miss, boolean, non-official host) and has no case for an absent cache field.
findings.location: src/ios/Providers/OpenAI/DeepSeekRequestUsage.swift:12-23 (parse guard) and src/ios/Providers/OpenAI/OpenAIAgentProvider.swift:268-271 / 808-811 (call sites passing the raw usage dictionary).

findings.certainty: high on the code inconsistency; the user-visible impact requires an unusual base-URL entry, so practical frequency is low.
findings.evidence: DeepSeekBilling.supportsBaseURL (DeepSeekBilling.swift:175-205) explicitly returns false when the raw string contains whitespace/newlines, "?", "#", "@" or "\\", while ProviderInstance.effectiveCustomBaseURL trims whitespace and newlines (ProviderInstance.swift:171-176) and the provider factory passes that trimmed value into the URL builder. Identity and per-request pricing therefore key off a different string than the one actually used to reach the vendor, so recognition can disagree with the endpoint that served the reply.

findings.certainty: high on the facts (no cap/TTL/prune exists); the severity judgement is a low-confidence estimate because no measurement was possible.
findings.evidence: Every main-chat request (including each tool-loop iteration) inserts one session_cost_requests row (SessionCostLedger.swift:60-66) and the only reclamation is ON DELETE CASCADE when the session row is deleted (verified by SessionCostLedgerTests.testRequestsCannotChargeAnotherSessionAndDeleteCascades); there is no row-count limit, age limit or pruning job, and the design note only claims “单请求记录随会话删除级联清理”. Each request also adds roughly two writes and up to four bounded summary reads (begin, refreshSessionCostSummary after begin, ledger summary inside finish, refreshSessionCostSummary after finish), so cost is proportional to actual usage rather than to stream chunks or wall-clock time; the 1-row-per-request storage is a few hundred bytes each.
findings.location: src/ios/Providers/OpenAI/SessionCostLedger.swift:24-40 (CREATE TABLE session_cost_requests with only an index; no cap/TTL/prune) and :52-68 (one row per request); callers at src/ios/Agent/Chat/AIChatViewModel+SSEStream.swift:275; per-request extra reads at AIChatViewModel+Billing.swift:30/39/47 plus SessionCostLedger.summary inside begin/finish.

findings.verification: Static read of the schema, all insert/delete sites and the call sites; no runtime measurement of row counts, DB growth or CPU/energy. Judged as recorded resource impact, not as a required change: growth is bounded by genuine request volume and the per-request work is O(1), so I do not consider this an unjustified waste at current scale.

limitations: No test, build, simulator, device or network execution was performed; this is a static read-only review, so all runtime/UI claims are unverified. Unexecuted tests: the 24 XCTests added by this change (DeepSeekBillingTests, DeepSeekRequestUsageTests, SessionCostLedgerTests, DeepSeekBalanceModelTests) were not run by me; task.md states they passed but also states they were run inside a temporary SwiftPM package using copied sources with matching SHA-256, without launching the iOS app, so the Xcode MinisTests target result and any integration with the app module remain unproven. No test at all covers processStreamEvents begin/finish wiring (AIChatViewModel+SSEStream.swift:275/986/1010), ChatStore.enroll/begin/finishSessionCostRequest against the real ChatStore connection (ChatStore.swift:958/1077/4255-4262), ON DELETE CASCADE on the production session table, showsSessionBilling gating, the fixed section order, or the four balance UI states (loading/failed/updated/not-applicable), and no device or real-account end-to-end check exists (task.md 目标与验收 is still unchecked and its 待完成 section says so). Unread or unresolved required Spec dependencies: .agents/skills/plan-task/SKILL.md is listed as 必读 in the task's Spec 阅读清单 but is excluded from this snapshot (whole .agents path excluded), so it could not be read; docs/harness/record-formats.md and docs/harness/operations.md were only seen through search excerpts (Pi authorization/naming), not read in full; the DeepSeek official pricing page https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/quick_start/pricing/ and https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/get-user-balance/ named in task.md are not in the snapshot and were not retrievable offline, so the price constants (flash 0.04/2/8 CNY per M, pro 0.30/9/27), the peak windows (weekday 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00 Asia/Shanghai; everything else, weekends and listed statutory holidays, at a uniform 0.5 multiplier), the hardcoded model IDs (deepseek-flash, deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp, deepseek-v4-pro) and the per-family effective dates (flash 2026-09-10 12:00, pro 2026-08-17) are only internally self-consistent with the tests and cannot be confirmed against the vendor. Additional unresolved dependencies: src/ios/Views/Providers is excluded from the snapshot, so I could not confirm that the app's official-DeepSeek entry actually sets customBaseURL to https://api.deepseek.com (required by DeepSeekPricing.supports/baseURL matching since there is no deepseek providerType) nor that the model catalog IDs match the hardcoded family list; if either differs, every DeepSeek session would silently display “—”. The 2026 statutory-holiday/make-up-day table and the assumption that off-peak is a flat 50% on all three token components are project decisions that could not be cross-checked. No measurement of runtime CPU/memory/energy/disk impact was possible, so the resource-efficiency conclusions are static only.
